text: Hana. I teach here on Tuesdays, and watch on every other day.
Play somebody first. I'd rather see a game of yours than hear you describe one.
I watched that game. Don't look alarmed -- I watch everyone's, it's the only way to know what to teach.
There were two or three moves in it you played because you were frightened, rather than because you had a reason. You will know the ones.
And the answer was the same every time, and you couldn't see it, because nobody has shown it to you yet.
So. The first thing, before openings, before shape, before any of it.
A group of stones lives by its liberties -- the empty points touching it. Fill the last one, and the group comes off the board.
Everything else in this game is a consequence of that sentence.
Let me set you a position. Black to play, and there is exactly one move that matters.
The board will keep. So will I.
The position is still on the small board. Black to play.
Good. Now say it back to me in your own words, silently, so I don't have to hear it.
That is the whole of your first lesson: count the liberties before you decide anything else.
You are a member here now, as far as I'm concerned. Come on Tuesdays. Bring the disasters.
There's a card in the tin by the kettle with your name on it. Marguerite insists on cards.

Now. I only drink here on Tuesdays. The rest of the week I am at the Essenveld Instituut, two stops north, where about thirty people your age are trying to become professionals and most of them will not.
They take beginners. That is not a kindness -- it is that they would rather build somebody from nothing than correct somebody's ten years of bad habits.
You have had one week of Go and you have already stopped being frightened of a losing position. That is rarer than talent and it cannot be taught.
Tram 4, northbound, from the stop at the end of the street. Ask for Marguerite at the desk. Tell her I sent you.
Go and pack the board. You'll want your own.
The road east, past the noticeboard. Marguerite is at the desk and she does not like being kept waiting, which is her whole personality.
You found it. Good.
The demonstration board at the front is where I teach. Use it whenever you like -- I would rather you took a class twice than pretended you had understood it once.
The rest of your time is yours. Play people. Lose to them. Come back.
Good. Say it back to yourself in your own words, silently, so I do not have to hear it.
That is the shape of every class here: I set you something, you count, and then you know it rather than having been told it.
